criteria.justification: The response explicitly diagnoses the issue as 'a governance problem wearing a naming costume' and analyzes why each round failed for a different reason rather than treating round four as an isolated naming choice.

Proposes assigning 'a single decision owner with cross-family authority' and a rule that future reopens require violating pre-agreed criteria, culminating in 'Ship it as final... and treat further churn as a documented backlog item, not a blocker.'

Notes each prior objection was genuinely new rather than repeated ('each round satisfies the previous objection and gets shot down by a new one'), and institutes a rule that only pre-agreed criteria violations count as valid reopens going forward, implicitly filtering out re-litigation.
Explicitly references the API field as 'locked and out of scope' when justifying why the name doesn't need to carry all explanatory weight and can be supplemented by tooltips instead.

Explicitly states 'Picking a fourth candidate name without fixing this just produces a fourth reopening' and restructures the approach around establishing a conceptual model and joint criteria before generating any candidate name, rather than repeating ad hoc naming attempts.
